skills.name: Standard deviation
skills.wrong_turn: Don't forget to square. For 2, 4, 6 the deviations from the mean 4 are −2, 0, 2, which add to 0. Square them first: the variance is (4+0+43)=(83), not 0.

skills.name: Summary statistics

steps.d: adding to or scaling the data

skills.wrong_turn: Adding a constant moves the center, not the spread. Add 10 to every score and the mean rises by 10, but the standard deviation stays the same, not 10 more.

skills.name: z-scores
skills.wrong_turn: Subtract first, then divide. For x=80, μ=70, σ=5: z=(80−705)=2, not 80−(705)=66.

skills.name: Random variables
skills.wrong_turn: E(X) is not the most likely value. For a die, E(X)=3.5, a value that never comes up.

skills.name: The binomial setting
skills.wrong_turn: Drawing without replacement is not binomial. Draw 5 cards and count hearts: after a heart, the chance of the next heart drops from (1352) to (1251), so p is not fixed.

skills.name: Binomial probabilities
skills.wrong_turn: 'At least 1' is not P(X=1). For 4 dice, P(at least one six)=1−((56))4≈0.518, not P(X=1)≈0.386.

skills.name: Binomial mean & spread
skills.wrong_turn: The standard deviation is np(1−p), not np(1−p). For n=100, p=0.5: σ=25=5, not 25.

skills.name: The normal distribution
skills.wrong_turn: The 68–95–99.7 rule counts both sides. About 95% of values lie within 2 standard deviations of the mean, so about 2.5% lie above μ+2σ, not 5%.

skills.name: Normal probabilities
skills.wrong_turn: Table values are areas to the left. For z=1, P(Z≤1)≈0.8413, so P(Z≥1)≈0.1587, not 0.8413.

skills.name: Scatter plots & correlation
skills.wrong_turn: Correlation is not causation. Ice cream sales and drownings rise together, but hot weather drives both; banning ice cream won't prevent drownings.
